title: Marginal zone lymphoma
subtitle: The antigen-driven lymphoma — extranodal (MALT), splenic and nodal MZL share a CD5−/CD10− phenotype but not a treatment. Find and treat the driver first (H. pylori, HCV, C. psittaci), irradiate localized disease with curative intent, and reserve systemic therapy for disseminated or symptomatic disease
source: Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (NCCN; WHO-HAEM5; EGILS) verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Three (now four) entities — WHO-HAEM5
rows: Arises in mucosa made lymphoid by chronic antigen. Stomach most common; then ocular adnexa, lung, salivary gland, thyroid, skin, breast, dura, small bowel. Lymphoepithelial lesions. Usually localized — often curable locally

Spleen + marrow (intrasinusoidal) ± blood; splenomegaly, cytopenias, villous lymphocytes, small IgM paraprotein, autoimmune cytopenias. Nodes uncommon. HCV-linked subset. del(7q), NOTCH2, KLF2 mutations
Nodes only (no extranodal or splenic primary). Behaves and is treated like FL
Split off as its own entity in WHO-HAEM5; very indolent, skin-directed therapy. Borrelia link in European series
blocks.footnote: All are CD5− CD10− small B cells, but genetics differ by site: t(11;18)(q21;q21) BIRC3::MALT1 in gastric and lung MALT; TNFAIP3 loss in ocular adnexa; GPR34 in salivary gland; FAS in cutaneous MZL; KMT2D, NOTCH2, KLF2 in nodal MZL. Also t(14;18)(q32;q21) IGH::MALT1, t(1;14) IGH::BCL10, t(3;14) IGH::FOXP1.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Every MZL: HCV antibody + RNA, HBsAg + anti-HBc, HIV, SPEP/immunofixation (paraprotein common), LDH, β2M
Gastric: EGD with multiple biopsies (map the stomach), H. pylori by histology + stool antigen or breath test (serology if on PPI), EUS for depth and perigastric nodes, FISH for t(11;18)
Splenic: smear (villous lymphocytes), flow, marrow biopsy, CT; DAT and autoimmune screen
PET/CT is less reliable than in FL (MALT and SMZL are variably FDG-avid) — CT is acceptable; a hot focus raises concern for transformation
Autoimmune history (Sjögren, Hashimoto) and site-specific exams: ophthalmology, ENT, thyroid ultrasound

blocks.heading: Antigen driver → antimicrobial first
rows: Eradication is first therapy for localized disease. Remission 77.5% (32 studies, 1,408 pts): stage I 78% vs II1 56%; mucosa/submucosa 82% vs deeper 54%; t(11;18)+ only 22% vs 78%
Doxycycline 3 wk: ORR 65%, 5-yr PFS 55% (phase 2, stage I); better if Cp eradicated (86% vs 47%). Cp DNA in 89% of that Italian cohort — prevalence varies widely by region
α-heavy-chain disease; early disease regresses with antibiotics
Antiviral therapy first if no urgent indication: 7/9 CR after interferon with HCV clearance, none in HCV− (Hermine, NEJM 2002); DAAs — SVR 98%, lymphoma response 73% in MZL (Arcaini, Blood 2016)
Autoimmune drive — no antimicrobial; treat by stage

blocks.heading: Staging gastric MALT — Lugano (GI) system
rows: Confined to the GI tract (single or multiple non-contiguous lesions)
Into the abdomen: local (perigastric) nodes / distant (mesenteric, para-aortic) nodes
Penetrates serosa into adjacent organs or tissues
Disseminated extranodal, or supradiaphragmatic nodes. No stage III
blocks.footnote: Non-gastric and nodal/splenic disease: Ann Arbor/Lugano.

blocks.heading: Small B-cell differential
rows: Diagnosis of exclusion; cyclin D1−, MYD88 usually wild-type
CD11c, CD25, CD103, CD123, annexin A1; BRAF V600E
blocks.footnote: Splenic MZL vs hairy cell: SMZL villi are short and polar, CD25−/annexin−/BRAF wild-type, and the marrow is intrasinusoidal and nodular; HCL has circumferential projections, a “dry tap”, monocytopenia. Splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli (WHO-HAEM5; absorbs HCL-variant) is CD25−, annexin−, TRAP−, CD123−. Splenic diffuse red pulp lymphoma is the other mimic.

blocks.heading: MALT-IPI — 1 point each
blocks.footnote: Age ≥70 · stage III–IV · LDH >ULN. Derived in IELSG-19 (n=401), validated in 633; prognostic in gastric and non-gastric disease (Thieblemont, Blood 2017).

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — treatment pathway, systemic therapy, dosing

boxes: confirm cure (breath/stool) ≥4 wk after, PPI off
Re-endoscope at ~3 months, then q3–6 mo
persistent but stable, HP-negative: keep watching
R-CHOP rarely (bulky, or concern for large cells)

blocks.heading: Systemic therapy — evidence and status
rows: IELSG-19 (MALT, n=454): 5-yr EFS 68% R-chlorambucil vs 50% rituximab vs 51% chlorambucil; PFS better; OS ~90% in all arms
Phase 2 MALT data (Salar, Blood 2017) and StiL NHL1 (which included MZL) support BR as the usual frontline chemo-immunotherapy for advanced disease
GALLIUM MZL subgroup (n=195): no PFS benefit (4-yr 72.6% vs 64.1%) and more grade 5 AEs (14.9% vs 9.7%) — use rituximab
MAGNOLIA (single arm, n=68): ORR 68%, CR 26%; 24-mo PFS 71%. AF 3%. Confirmatory MAHOGANY (zanubrutinib + rituximab vs R²) still ongoing; approval remains accelerated
PCYC-1121 ORR 48% led to 2017 accelerated approval; SELENE (FL/MZL, + chemo) missed PFS → withdrawn
AUGMENT included 63 MZL; overall PFS HR 0.46 — but the MZL subgroup showed no significant PFS benefit (small, imbalanced). Approved nonetheless
TRANSCEND FL MZL cohort (single arm; nodal 48%, splenic 27%, MALT 25%): ORR 95% of 66 infused (84% of all leukapheresed, per label), CR 56% ITT; grade 3 CRS / neuro 4% each
ZUMA-5 MZL cohort: ORR 77%, median PFS not reached at 3 yr
Umbralisib MZL/FL approval withdrawn 2022 (excess deaths). No bispecific is approved for MZL

blocks.html: Transformation to DLBCL is uncommon but prognostically important: suspect with rising LDH, a rapidly growing or FDG-hot lesion, B symptoms. Biopsy, then treat as DLBCL. Scattered large cells in a MALT lymphoma are not by themselves transformation — sheets are.

blocks.heading: Key evidence
rows: HCV clearance regresses splenic MZL (IFN; DAAs 73%)
R-chlorambucil > either alone for EFS; OS equal
Obinutuzumab: no PFS gain, more fatal AEs
R²: benefit driven by FL, not MZL

blocks.heading: After eradication — restaging endoscopy
rows: Asymptomatic and stable: keep observing (≥12 mo). Symptomatic or progressing: ISRT
Second-line eradication; ISRT if progressing or symptomatic

blocks.heading: Splenic MZL — practical points
items: Many never need treatment — observe asymptomatic, stable disease
Rituximab alone has largely replaced splenectomy as first therapy: high response rates, no surgical risk. Splenectomy remains diagnostic and therapeutic when tissue is needed or rituximab fails
Before splenectomy: pneumococcal, meningococcal (ACWY + B) and Hib vaccines ≥2 weeks before — and before rituximab, which blunts vaccine response
Treat autoimmune cytopenias as part of the disease — they often respond to rituximab

blocks.heading: Dosing
rows: PPI BID + bismuth subsalicylate 524 mg QID + tetracycline 500 mg QID + metronidazole 500 mg TID–QID, 14 days
375 mg/m² weekly ×4; maintenance 375 q8wk ×2 yr optional
Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1+2 + rituximab 375 d1, q28d ×6
Chlorambucil 6 mg/m²/d PO wk 1–6, then 2-wk blocks (wk 9–10, 13–14, 17–18, 21–22) + rituximab 375 wk 1–4, 9, 13, 17, 21
160 mg BID or 320 mg daily, continuous
Lenalidomide 20 mg d1–21 q28d ×12 + rituximab weekly C1, d1 C2–5

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: Always test for the driver — H. pylori, HCV — before any cytotoxic therapy
t(11;18) predicts H. pylori non-response (and dissemination): go to RT rather than repeated antibiotics
Give gastric MALT time: histologic regression after eradication can take a year or more
MYD88 L265P favors LPL; CD5+ or cyclin D1+ is not MZL
